index 0000000..64b7b73
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/contract/compose/inter_plane_wire_rows_test.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,323 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Copyright 2026 The Stargate Authors
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+#
+# inter_plane_wire_rows_test.sh: hermetic fixtures for the decision rules of
+# the RUNTIME rows in inter_plane_wire_test.sh (T196 Acceptance 1).
+#
+# Why: the runtime rows were lifted by T045 but never ran against a live stack
+# until the T155 pass, which found that R2/R3 opened Unix sockets with bash
+# `exec 3<>`, which always fails with ENXIO (R2 could never pass and R3 could
+# never fail), that R5 read wireprobe's exit 0 ("the bad major was rejected") as
+# "accepted", that R7 read the host-network DP's /proc/<pid>/net and blamed the DP
+# for every host listener, and that every row printed PASS after a finding. A
+# live run alone cannot show that a row's verdict can fail, so these fixtures run
+# the REAL gate script, black-box, against a stub `docker` with discriminating
+# negative controls.
+#
+# Mechanics: the gate runs from a symlink farm of the repository (so its build
+# placeholder lands in a private target/), with stub `docker` and `git` first on
+# PATH. The stub executes each `docker run` command LOCALLY, rewriting
+# /run/stargate to a fixture directory: in-group UIDs (5101/5102/0) see
+# ingroup/, any other UID sees outgroup/. The fixture sets each directory's
+# socket modes to model what the kernel tells that caller (0660 connects, 0000
+# is EACCES, 0666 is a world-dialable socket). The dialer program itself is the
+# gate's, unmodified; only its container is emulated. wireprobe verdicts come
+# from a per-scenario exit-code table, and `docker inspect` returns the pid of a
+# fixture "DP" process whose TCP listeners the fixture controls, beside a
+# foreign listener in the same network namespace that R7 must not attribute.
+
+set -uo pipefail
+
+REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
+GATE="$REPO_ROOT/tests/contract/compose/inter_plane_wire_test.sh"
+for tool in python3 perl jq; do
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "FAIL: $tool is required by the wire-row fixtures" >&2; exit 1; }
+done
+if [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]; then
+  # Root bypasses the file-mode checks the EACCES fixtures depend on.
+  echo "FAIL: run inter_plane_wire_rows_test.sh as an unprivileged user" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+FX="$(mktemp -d)"
+PIDS=()
+cleanup() {
+  for pid in "${PIDS[@]}"; do kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null; wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null; done
+  rm -rf "$FX"
+}
+trap cleanup EXIT
+
+errs=()
+bail() { errs+=("$*"); }
+
+# --- symlink farm: real sources, private target/ -----------------------------
+mkdir -p "$FX/root/target" "$FX/bin" "$FX/ingroup" "$FX/outgroup"
+for entry in "$REPO_ROOT"/* "$REPO_ROOT"/.[!.]*; do
+  name="$(basename "$entry")"
+  case "$name" in target|.git|'.[!.]*') continue ;; esac
+  ln -s "$entry" "$FX/root/$name"
+done
+
+cat > "$FX/compose.json" <<'EOF'
+{"volumes": {"stargate-ipc": {"name": "fx_stargate-ipc"}, "stargate-keys": {"name": "fx_stargate-keys"}},
+ "services": {"stargate-control": {"volumes": [{"source": "stargate-keys", "target": "/etc/stargate/keys"}]},
+              "stargate-dp": {"volumes": [{"source": "stargate-keys", "target": "/etc/stargate/keys"}]}}}
+EOF
+
+cat > "$FX/bin/git" <<EOF
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+if [ "\$*" = "rev-parse --show-toplevel" ]; then echo "$FX/root"; exit 0; fi
+exec "$(command -v git)" "\$@"
+EOF
+
+cat > "$FX/bin/docker" <<'EOF'
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Stub Docker for the wire-row fixtures. Unknown shapes fail loudly (97) so a
+# gate change cannot silently stop exercising the fixtures.
+set -uo pipefail
+case "${1:-}" in
+  compose)
+    shift
+    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do case "$1" in -f|--env-file|-p) shift 2 ;; *) break ;; esac; done
+    case "$*" in
+      "config --format json") cat "$WIRE_FX/compose.json" ;;
+      "ps --status running --services") printf 'stargate-dp\nstargate-control\n' ;;
+      "ps -q stargate-dp") echo fxdpcid ;;
+      *) echo "stub docker: unhandled compose $*" >&2; exit 97 ;;
+    esac ;;
+  inspect)
+    [ "$*" = "inspect -f {{.State.Pid}} fxdpcid" ] || { echo "stub docker: unhandled $*" >&2; exit 97; }
+    cat "$WIRE_FX/dp.pid" ;;
+  run)
+    shift
+    user=""
+    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
+      case "$1" in
+        --rm) shift ;;
+        --user|-v|-w|--network) [ "$1" = "--user" ] && user="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+        *) break ;;
+      esac
+    done
+    shift # image
+    case "$user" in 5101:*|5102:*|0:*|"") ipc="$WIRE_FX/ingroup" ;; *) ipc="$WIRE_FX/outgroup" ;; esac
+    args=()
+    for a in "$@"; do a="${a//\/run\/stargate/$ipc}"; a="${a//\/src\//$PWD/}"; args+=("$a"); done
+    case "${args[0]}" in
+      stat)
+        case "${args[-1]}" in
+          */dp.sock) echo "660 5102 5100" ;;
+          */control.sock) echo "660 5101 5100" ;;
+          *) exit 97 ;;
+        esac ;;
+      go)
+        out=""
+        for ((i = 0; i < ${#args[@]}; i++)); do [ "${args[$i]}" = "-o" ] && out="${args[$((i + 1))]}"; done
+        [ -n "$out" ] || exit 97
+        printf '#!/bin/sh\nexit 97\n' > "$out" ;;
+      */stargate-wireprobe)
+        key="${args[1]}"
+        for ((i = 2; i < ${#args[@]}; i++)); do
+          case "${args[$i]}" in -major|-minor) key="$key:${args[$((i + 1))]}" ;; esac
+        done
+        code="$(awk -v k="$key" '$1 == k { print $2 }' "$WIRE_FX/probe.table")"
+        exit "${code:-0}" ;;
+      *) exec "${args[@]}" ;;
+    esac ;;
+  *) echo "stub docker: unhandled $*" >&2; exit 97 ;;
+esac
+EOF
+chmod 0755 "$FX/bin/git" "$FX/bin/docker"
+
+# --- fixture processes -----------------------------------------------------
+# Unix listeners: connect(2) completes against the backlog without accept().
+# A path in $SATURATE_FX gets a zero backlog that one held connection fills,
+# so a further blocking connect(2) never completes (a wedged peer).
+start_uds() {
+  SATURATE_FX="${SATURATE_FX:-}" python3 -c '
+import os, socket, sys, time
+held = []
+saturate = os.environ["SATURATE_FX"].split()
+for path in sys.argv[1:]:
+    s = socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
+    s.bind(path)
+    s.listen(0 if path in saturate else 16)
+    held.append(s)
+    if path in saturate:
+        filler = socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
+        filler.connect(path)
+        held.append(filler)
+print("READY", flush=True)
+time.sleep(3600)
+' "$@" > "$FX/uds.ready" &
+  PIDS+=("$!")
+}
+# TCP listeners on ephemeral loopback ports; prints the ports it holds.
+start_tcp() { # start_tcp <count> <portfile>
+  python3 -c '
+import socket, sys, time
+held = []
+for _ in range(int(sys.argv[1])):
+    s = socket.socket()
+    s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
+    s.listen(4)
+    held.append(s)
+print(" ".join(str(s.getsockname()[1]) for s in held), flush=True)
+time.sleep(3600)
+' "$1" > "$2" &
+  PIDS+=("$!")
+  LAST_PID="$!"
+}
+await_file() { # await_file <file>
+  local i=0
+  while [ ! -s "$1" ] && [ "$i" -lt 100 ]; do sleep 0.05; i=$((i + 1)); done
+  [ -s "$1" ] || { echo "FAIL: fixture process did not start ($1)" >&2; exit 1; }
+}
+stop_all() {
+  for pid in "${PIDS[@]}"; do kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null; wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null; done
+  PIDS=()
+  rm -f "$FX"/ingroup/*.sock "$FX"/outgroup/*.sock "$FX"/*.ready "$FX"/*.ports "$FX/dp.pid"
+}
+
+# setup <outgroup-mode|missing> <ingroup-control-mode> <dp-listener-count> <probe-table>
+setup() {
+  stop_all
+  start_uds "$FX/ingroup/dp.sock" "$FX/ingroup/control.sock" "$FX/outgroup/dp.sock" "$FX/outgroup/control.sock"
+  await_file "$FX/uds.ready"
+  chmod 0660 "$FX/ingroup/dp.sock"
+  chmod "$2" "$FX/ingroup/control.sock"
+  if [ "$1" = missing ]; then
+    rm -f "$FX/outgroup/dp.sock"
+    chmod 0000 "$FX/outgroup/control.sock"
+  else
+    chmod "$1" "$FX/outgroup/dp.sock" "$FX/outgroup/control.sock"
+  fi
+  start_tcp 1 "$FX/foreign.ports"   # another process's listener in this namespace
+  await_file "$FX/foreign.ports"
+  start_tcp "$3" "$FX/dp.ports"
+  DP_PID="$LAST_PID"
+  if [ "$3" -gt 0 ]; then await_file "$FX/dp.ports"; else sleep 0.3; fi
+  echo "$DP_PID" > "$FX/dp.pid"
+  # The "proxy port" is the DP fixture's first listener (8881 may be in use here).
+  PROXY_PORT_FX="$(cut -d' ' -f1 "$FX/dp.ports" 2>/dev/null)"
+  printf '%s\n' "$4" | tr ',' '\n' | sed 's/=/ /' > "$FX/probe.table"
+}
+
+run_gate() { # run_gate <label>; a hung gate (exit 124) fails the scenario
+  GATE_OUT="$(cd "$FX/root" && PATH="$FX/bin:$PATH" WIRE_FX="$FX" \
+    STARGATE_WIRE_PROXY_PORT="${PROXY_PORT_FX:-1}" timeout 180 bash "$GATE" 2>&1)"
+  GATE_RC=$?
+  printf '%s\n' "$GATE_OUT" > "$FX/$1.log"
+}
+expect_rc() { [ "$GATE_RC" -eq "$2" ] || bail "[$1] gate exit $GATE_RC, want $2"; }
+# Here-strings, not `printf | grep -q`: under pipefail an early grep exit can
+# SIGPIPE the writer and flip the verdict.
+expect_line() { grep -qE "$2" <<< "$GATE_OUT" || bail "[$1] missing /$2/ in gate output"; }
+expect_no_line() { ! grep -qE "$2" <<< "$GATE_OUT" || bail "[$1] unexpected /$2/ in gate output"; }
+show_on_failure() { [ "${#errs[@]}" -eq "$2" ] || { echo "--- [$1] gate output ---" >&2; cat "$FX/$1.log" >&2; }; }
+
+# --- S1 positive control: every runtime row must be able to PASS -----------
+n="${#errs[@]}"
+setup 0000 0660 1 ""
+run_gate s1
+expect_rc s1 0
+for row in R1 R2 R3 R4 R5 R6 R7; do
+  expect_line s1 "^$row: PASS"
+  expect_no_line s1 "^$row: FAIL"
+done
+expect_line s1 '^R8: SKIP'
+expect_line s1 '^R9: SKIP'
+foreign="$(cat "$FX/foreign.ports")"
+expect_no_line s1 "R7: .*\\b$foreign\\b"
+show_on_failure s1 "$n"
+
+# --- S2 R3 negative control: a world-dialable socket must fail R3 ----------
+n="${#errs[@]}"
+setup 0666 0660 1 ""
+run_gate s2
+expect_rc s2 1
+expect_line s2 '^R3: FAIL'
+expect_no_line s2 '^R3: PASS'
+expect_line s2 '^R2: PASS'
+show_on_failure s2 "$n"
+
+# --- S3 R3: a refusal that is not EACCES (missing socket) is not a PASS ----
+n="${#errs[@]}"
+setup missing 0660 1 ""
+run_gate s3
+expect_rc s3 1
+expect_line s3 '^R3: FAIL'
+expect_no_line s3 '^R3: PASS'
+show_on_failure s3 "$n"
+
+# --- S4 R2 negative control: the peer UID cannot dial its socket ----------
+n="${#errs[@]}"
+setup 0000 0000 1 ""
+run_gate s4
+expect_rc s4 1
+expect_line s4 '^R2: FAIL'
+expect_no_line s4 '^R2: PASS'
+show_on_failure s4 "$n"
+
+# --- S5 R5: wireprobe exit 0 means the rule held; non-zero must fail -------
+for table in "major:2=1" "major:0=1" "major:1=1" "nomajor=1"; do
+  label="s5-${table%%=*}"
+  label="${label//:/-}"
+  n="${#errs[@]}"
+  setup 0000 0660 1 "$table"
+  run_gate "$label"
+  expect_rc "$label" 1
+  expect_line "$label" '^R5: FAIL'
+  expect_no_line "$label" '^R5: PASS'
+  expect_line "$label" '^R6: PASS'
+  show_on_failure "$label" "$n"
+done
+
+# --- S6 R7: a second DP listener must fail; the foreign one never counts ---
+n="${#errs[@]}"
+setup 0000 0660 2 ""
+run_gate s6
+expect_rc s6 1
+expect_line s6 '^R7: FAIL'
+expect_no_line s6 '^R7: PASS'
+second="$(cut -d' ' -f2 "$FX/dp.ports")"
+expect_line s6 "R7: .*\\b$second\\b"
+show_on_failure s6 "$n"
+
+# --- S7 R7: a DP with no TCP listener is a sanity failure, not a PASS ------
+n="${#errs[@]}"
+setup 0000 0660 0 ""
+run_gate s7
+expect_rc s7 1
+expect_line s7 '^R7: FAIL'
+expect_no_line s7 '^R7: PASS'
+show_on_failure s7 "$n"
+
+# --- S8 R2: a wedged peer (full accept queue) is a bounded FAIL, not a hang --
+n="${#errs[@]}"
+SATURATE_FX="$FX/ingroup/control.sock" setup 0000 0660 1 ""
+run_gate s8
+expect_rc s8 1
+expect_line s8 '^R2: FAIL'
+expect_no_line s8 '^R2: PASS'
+expect_line s8 'R2: uid 5102 .*exit 124'
+show_on_failure s8 "$n"
+
+# --- S9 R3: a dial timeout never counts as EACCES ---------------------------
+n="${#errs[@]}"
+SATURATE_FX="$FX/outgroup/dp.sock $FX/outgroup/control.sock" setup 0666 0660 1 ""
+run_gate s9
+expect_rc s9 1
+expect_line s9 '^R3: FAIL'
+expect_no_line s9 '^R3: PASS'
+expect_line s9 'R3: .*exit 124, not EACCES'
+show_on_failure s9 "$n"
+
+stop_all
+if [ "${#errs[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
+  printf 'FAIL: inter_plane_wire_rows_test.sh: %d assertion(s) failed:\n' "${#errs[@]}" >&2
+  for e in "${errs[@]}"; do printf '  - %s\n' "$e" >&2; done
+  exit 1
+fi
+echo "PASS: inter_plane_wire_rows_test.sh: R2/R3 bounded real dialer, R5 exit semantics, R7 process attribution and per-row PASS discipline hold."
+exit 0
diff --git a/tests/contract/compose/inter_plane_wire_test.sh b/tests/contract/compose/inter_plane_wire_test.sh
index 173da49..c1607cf 100755
--- a/tests/contract/compose/inter_plane_wire_test.sh
+++ b/tests/contract/compose/inter_plane_wire_test.sh
@@ -426,6 +426,18 @@ else
   # until a `stargate init` compose stack is up, and FAILs (bail) when the
   # stack IS up and the property breaks. R8/R9 additionally require
   # STARGATE_WIRE_RUNTIME_MUTATE=1 — they restart/rotate a live stack.
+  # T196: a row prints PASS only when it recorded no finding (row_begin /
+  # row_end); the decision rules are pinned by inter_plane_wire_rows_test.sh,
+  # which runs this script against a stub Docker with negative controls.
+  row_begin() { ROW_ERRS="${#errs[@]}"; }
+  row_end() { # row_end <row> <what passed>
+    local found=$(( ${#errs[@]} - ROW_ERRS ))
+    if [ "$found" -eq 0 ]; then
+      echo "$1: PASS ($2)" >&2
+    else
+      echo "$1: FAIL ($found finding(s), listed below)" >&2
+    fi
+  }
 
   GOIMG="golang:1.26.3-bookworm@sha256:252599aeb51ad60b83e4d8821802068127c528c707cb7dd7afd93be057c6011c"
   IPC_VOL=""
@@ -436,14 +448,51 @@ else
   fi
 
   # svc_running <service>: true iff the compose service has a running container.
+  # T196: capture first. Under pipefail, `docker ... | grep -q` fails when grep
+  # exits on an early match and the writer then dies of SIGPIPE, which made a
+  # running stack SKIP rows at random.
   svc_running() {
-    docker compose -f "$COMPOSE" --env-file "$ENV_FILE" ps --status running --services 2>/dev/null | grep -qx "$1"
+    local services
+    services="$(docker compose -f "$COMPOSE" --env-file "$ENV_FILE" ps --status running --services 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
+    grep -qx "$1" <<< "$services"
   }
   # ipc_run <uid:gid> <cmd...>: cmd in the pinned golang image with the IPC
   # volume at /run/stargate, as the given uid:gid.
   ipc_run() {
     docker run --rm --user "$1" -v "$IPC_VOL:/run/stargate" "$GOIMG" "${@:2}"
   }
+  # uds_dial <uid:gid> <socket>: a real connect(2) on a Unix stream socket as
+  # that identity (T196). bash `exec 3<>` cannot open a socket (ENXIO), so the
+  # rows use perl's socket API (perl-base ships in the pinned image). Exit 0 =
+  # connected, 13 = EACCES, 1 = any other connect error, 3 = no socket.
+  UDS_DIAL_PL='use Socket; socket(my $s, PF_UNIX, SOCK_STREAM, 0) or exit 3; connect($s, pack_sockaddr_un($ARGV[0])) and exit 0; exit($!{EACCES} ? 13 : 1);'
+  uds_dial() {
+    ipc_run "$1" perl -e "$UDS_DIAL_PL" "$2"
+  }
+  # The proxy port R7 allows. Overridable only so the hermetic fixture can
+  # use a free ephemeral port; any other listener still fails the row.
+  PROXY_PORT="${STARGATE_WIRE_PROXY_PORT:-8881}"
+  # dp_listen_ports <pid>: decimal ports of TCP LISTEN sockets OWNED by that
+  # process (T196). The DP runs in the host network namespace, so
+  # /proc/<pid>/net/tcp{,6} lists every host listener; only rows whose socket
+  # inode appears among the process's own descriptors belong to the DP.
+  # Reading another UID's /proc/<pid>/fd needs root; failure returns 2.
+  # LISTEN state is 0A; the port is the hex field after the final ':' of
+  # local_address; field 10 is the socket inode. Hex→dec conversion is shell
+  # printf (POSIX), not awk strtonum — a gawk extension absent from
+  # mawk/busybox awk (T045 review round-1 follow-up).
+  dp_listen_ports() {
+    local pid="$1" fd target inodes=""
+    ls "/proc/$pid/fd" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 2
+    for fd in "/proc/$pid/fd"/*; do
+      target="$(readlink "$fd" 2>/dev/null)" || continue
+      case "$target" in socket:\[*\]) inodes="$inodes ${target//[^0-9]/}" ;; esac
+    done
+    awk -v inodes="$inodes" 'BEGIN { n = split(inodes, list, " "); for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) own[list[i]] = 1 }
+      $4 == "0A" && ($10 in own) { split($2, a, ":"); print a[2] }' \
+      "/proc/$pid/net/tcp" "/proc/$pid/net/tcp6" 2>/dev/null |
+      while IFS= read -r hex; do printf '%d\n' "0x$hex"; done | sort -un
+  }
   # need_stack <row>: SKIP-guard — both planes running and both sockets
   # present (the properties under test need the real UDS topology).
   need_stack() {
@@ -504,104 +553,110 @@ else
 
 # LIFT-MARKER: R1
   if need_stack "R1"; then # socket mode 0660, owner stargate-{cp,dp}:stargate-ipc (control-grpc.md §"Socket topology"; wire-auth.md §6.1)
+    row_begin
     dp_stat="$(ipc_run 0:0 stat -c '%a %u %g' /run/stargate/dp.sock)" || bail "R1: cannot stat dp.sock in the stargate-ipc volume"
     [ "$dp_stat" = "660 5102 5100" ] || bail "R1: dp.sock is '$dp_stat', want '660 5102 5100' (mode 0660, stargate-dp:stargate-ipc)"
     cp_stat="$(ipc_run 0:0 stat -c '%a %u %g' /run/stargate/control.sock)" || bail "R1: cannot stat control.sock in the stargate-ipc volume"
     [ "$cp_stat" = "660 5101 5100" ] || bail "R1: control.sock is '$cp_stat', want '660 5101 5100' (mode 0660, stargate-cp:stargate-ipc)"
-    echo "R1: PASS (sockets 0660, owned stargate-{dp,cp}:stargate-ipc)" >&2
+    row_end R1 "sockets 0660, owned stargate-{dp,cp}:stargate-ipc"
   fi
 
 # LIFT-MARKER: R2
   if need_stack "R2"; then # peer-plane UID connect(2) succeeds on its dial-direction socket (control-grpc.md invariant row 5)
-    if ! ipc_run 5102:5100 timeout 2 bash -c 'exec 3<>/run/stargate/control.sock' 2>/dev/null; then
-      bail "R2: DP uid (5102) cannot connect(2) control.sock — mode regressed below peer-dialable (0600-class), inter-plane comms silently broken"
-    fi
-    if ! ipc_run 5101:5100 timeout 2 bash -c 'exec 3<>/run/stargate/dp.sock' 2>/dev/null; then
-      bail "R2: CP uid (5101) cannot connect(2) dp.sock — mode regressed below peer-dialable (0600-class), inter-plane comms silently broken"
-    fi
-    echo "R2: PASS (peer-plane UIDs connect their dial-direction sockets)" >&2
+    row_begin
+    for dial in 5102:5100:control.sock 5101:5100:dp.sock; do
+      uds_dial "${dial%:*}" "/run/stargate/${dial##*:}"
+      rc=$?
+      [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || bail "R2: uid ${dial%%:*} cannot connect(2) ${dial##*:} (dialer exit $rc; 13 = EACCES) — mode regressed below peer-dialable (0600-class), inter-plane comms silently broken"
+    done
+    row_end R2 "peer-plane UIDs connect their dial-direction sockets"
   fi
 
 # LIFT-MARKER: R3
   if need_stack "R3"; then # non-group UID connect(2) fails with EACCES on both sockets (control-grpc.md invariant row 6)
+    row_begin
     for sock in dp.sock control.sock; do
-      if ipc_run 1234:1234 timeout 2 bash -c "exec 3<>/run/stargate/$sock" 2>/dev/null; then
-        bail "R3: out-of-group uid 1234 connected $sock — the mode/group scheme must narrow the dial surface (not 0666-equivalent)"
-      fi
+      uds_dial 1234:1234 "/run/stargate/$sock"
+      rc=$?
+      case "$rc" in
+        13) ;;
+        0) bail "R3: out-of-group uid 1234 connected $sock — the mode/group scheme must narrow the dial surface (not 0666-equivalent)" ;;
+        *) bail "R3: out-of-group uid 1234 dialing $sock ended with exit $rc, not EACCES — a missing socket or launcher failure does not prove the permission refusal" ;;
+      esac
     done
-    echo "R3: PASS (out-of-group UID gets EACCES on both sockets)" >&2
+    row_end R3 "out-of-group UID gets EACCES on both sockets"
   fi
 
 # LIFT-MARKER: R4
   if need_stack "R4"; then # wrong-key peer rejected at the TLS handshake (wire-auth.md §3.3; read-only probe)
-    if probe_run wrongkey -socket /run/stargate/dp.sock; then
-      echo "R4: PASS (rogue client key rejected at the dp.sock TLS handshake)" >&2
-    else
-      bail "R4: the DP did NOT abort a handshake from a key it does not pin — wire-auth.md §3.3 violated (silent auth bypass class)"
-    fi
+    row_begin

+#
+# inter_plane_wire_rows_test.sh: hermetic fixtures for the decision rules of
+# the RUNTIME rows in inter_plane_wire_test.sh (T196 Acceptance 1).
+#
+# Why: the runtime rows were lifted by T045 but never ran against a live stack
+# until the T155 pass, which found that R2/R3 opened Unix sockets with bash
+# `exec 3<>`, which always fails with ENXIO (R2 could never pass and R3 could
+# never fail), that R5 read wireprobe's exit 0 ("the bad major was rejected") as
+# "accepted", that R7 read the host-network DP's /proc/<pid>/net and blamed the DP
+# for every host listener, and that every row printed PASS after a finding. A
+# live run alone cannot show that a row's verdict can fail, so these fixtures run
+# the REAL gate script, black-box, against a stub `docker` with discriminating
+# negative controls.
+#
+# Mechanics: the gate runs from a symlink farm of the repository (so its build
+# placeholder lands in a private target/), with stub `docker` and `git` first on
+# PATH. The stub executes each `docker run` command LOCALLY, rewriting
+# /run/stargate to a fixture directory: in-group UIDs (5101/5102/0) see
+# ingroup/, any other UID sees outgroup/. The fixture sets each directory's
+# socket modes to model what the kernel tells that caller (0660 connects, 0000
+# is EACCES, 0666 is a world-dialable socket). The dialer program itself is the
+# gate's, unmodified; only its container is emulated. wireprobe verdicts come
+# from a per-scenario exit-code table, and `docker inspect` returns the pid of a
+# fixture "DP" process whose TCP listeners the fixture controls, beside a
+# foreign listener in the same network namespace that R7 must not attribute.
+
+set -uo pipefail
+

+  exit 1
